Starting from A (outlined), everything reachable lies in its component, the tinted region in the accent color holding A, B and C; D and E are faded. The card shows {A, B, C}." width="100%"} Returns every node reachable from `node` when edge direction is ignored (its weakly connected component on a directed graph). Use it to extract the part of a network a given entity belongs to, without computing every component. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node, as an ID or label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [set[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node IDs of its component, including `node`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A breadth-first search from the node over edges in both directions, $O(V + E)$ for the component found. Matches NetworkX's `node_connected_component` (undirected graphs only there). ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#9dfbfdc9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("D", "E")]) sorted(g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in g.node_connected_component("A")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C'] ``` ::: :::
